steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: You know, Master Edge, I'm kind of intrigued. What was Stitch's mentor like?

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: I just knew you had an ulterior motive for coming with me, you runt.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: You bother yourself with that Stitch boy an awful lot.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Hahah, you caught me red-handed.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: That's just the kind of guy I am, hoping for everyone to hit it off and make friends.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Then you'd love his mentor.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Finch Canvas was his name. Most well-loved architectural designer in all of Zeruertza.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: His style might've been leagues apart from the Durin vogue, but when he explained things, he always our hearts doing it.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: In his words, he'd, er, what was it...? Right, 'throw off our ceaseless desires.'

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: His arguments were unique, relatively, but the Zeruertzans loved him.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: So why would someone like him leave?

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: That's the mystery.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: He just up and went, and never told anyone.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: That's... pretty weird for sure.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: As for the apprentice he left behind... we all recognize his talent, but, well, you've seen how he acts.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Hahah. I bet it's to do with how his teacher suddenly left?

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: So we all reckon.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Oh? You got some results?

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Hrmm, let's take a look...

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Verdict?

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Ach. More or less how you predicted.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: We've got just under a month's time left.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: A month? Should be enough to enlarge the lifts, then.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Fancy meeting you here, Gavial.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Fancy me. Looks like you don't need me to pitch in anymore?

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Mmm. This about does it for the survey.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Did you win over Avdotya?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Sure did. She said she'll help talk the Zeruertzans into it.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Good. All that's left should be putting out the official city-wide notice of the situation.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: It's not just deciding how to head to the surface. We've got to settle the matter of the dome too.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Huh? What's up with the dome?

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Oh, silly me. Nearly forgot you aren't Durins.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Right. Calamity doesn't come for Durin cities so often, but it's a decent bet a Durin has his city wrecked at least once in his life.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: It doesn't haunt us to leave the homes we grew up in.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Contrarily, you see, we always make sure our cities are in the best condition before we leave them, so they greet destruction the finest they can be.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Wow, that kicks ass!

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: So you think? It's only natural for us.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: And no matter why that hole's been sitting in the dome all this time, we've got to do something about it now.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Yeah, speaking of the dome, where's Stitch?

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Eh? Wasn't he with you?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: What? He said he was gonna find you guys.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Gavial, do you need Stitch?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: You know where he went?

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Mm-hm. I met him when we came in. He didn't say anything to me, he just went outside the cave.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: You solemnly swear to us you have a map, and now you tell us that map's likely in some book on a shelf somewhere?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: (Clears throat) I can hardly do anything about that.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I've had no interest in returning to the surface, after all. You should be content with the fact I could remember once seeing a forebear's map recorded in a book.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: If that cave network turns out to be as complex as you say, then I don't mind spending a little more of the time we do have.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: So, do you still remember what exactly that book was called?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I've forgotten. I vaguely recall it should be a travel log, detailing the Durin author's variegated experiences on the surface.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: What's the point of asking, anyway? It's not as if we can read Durish.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: I can't, but don't forget. I've got my friends here.

steps.name: Strange Machine #0429
steps.text: Zumama. Zumama. Do you require help?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: I want to find this travel log Avdotya's talking about, with a map recording the route through the cave network to the surface.

steps.name: Strange Machine
steps.text: Library books: infrequently sorted. Difficulty of search: relatively high.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: If you find it, I'll give you all an intense round of maintenance.

steps.name: Strange Machine #0429
steps.text: Zumama: friend. Assist Zumama.

steps.name: Strange Machine
steps.text: Assist Zumama. Assist Zumama.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Fantastic. Take it away, then. I'll be waiting outside. Remember to shout for me if something gives you trouble.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Yep.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Also... High Priest.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Yes, I'm here.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Pitch in.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: What in the...?!

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: A friend of mine.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Shouldn't you have asked me first if I knew any Durish, Zumama?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Is there any way you wouldn't?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Oh. Are you still miffed I never told you about all this business underground?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: You see, Zumama, if I regaled you about every last thing I knew, you could figure out how to construct an entire nomadic city and build it too before I finished.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: I personally believe the pursuit of knowledge has to rest at some point, though I'm not a person per se.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Will you help or not?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: If you'll pardon me once I find it.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Deal.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Er, Inam, what are you standing at the library doors for?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: I'm waiting for someone. And you?

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Library caretaker called me over to discuss something about refurbishing the place.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: He's been wanting to, but never got around to it. Now's a good chance.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: I've been a little curious about that.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Plenty of time's passed since the broadcast, and, okay, none of the city's Durins are panicking, but...

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Why are some even planning to refurbish their buildings?

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Hm? Oh, right, you're a surface-dweller. I see, it would be lost on you.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: You have built those roving cities to avoid disasters, haven't you?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: But we're different, see. Our cities can't move about.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Nomadicizing cities built underground would be much more of a challenge, yes.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Between you and me, I've heard of masters who've had thoughts of building cities just like that.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: You see, if we fit rock-crushers and borer planes and the like onto the dome, and slipped a base plate under the whole city, it might just be within reach.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Er... I'm not great with construction, but that sounds even crazier than our nomadic cities are.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: And I've never heard of anyone looking to actually pull it off, truth be told.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Anywho, our cities don't move. Unnomadic, if you will.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: But. Every one of our cities does have Originium vein detector facilities, which send off an alert when one of them encroaches.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: I wonder if those sensors could replace the jobs of Catastrophe Messengers...

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: I've heard of them. It's not quite apples to apples, see, because the spread of Originium veins is the only thing our sensors can pick up on.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: True. Judging from what I've heard, there's also a stretch of time from vein discovery to vein activation, and outside of special circumstances like now, you'd plenty of time to evacuate.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: But if hints of a Catastrophe were detected, getting so much time to react would be a miracle.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Circling back—you're used to abandoning your own cities, then?

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Exactly the opposite, if I had to say.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Durins adore everything that ties to this land. We adore machinery, buildings, every city we build.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: But should disaster insist on its way, then our cities are bound to be destroyed.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: And if we're going to face up to that reality, then there's something we have to consider.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: A city's inhabitants leave it because of calamity, but calamity doesn't last forever. There'll be other Durins, maybe even our own offspring and theirs, who'll come upon that same land once again.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: They'll see the city's remains, they'll lament the disaster that befell it, but as the people who once lived and breathed in it, is that really all we want them to come and learn?

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Is surrender our only choice, in the face of our inescapable fate?

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: We don't accept that. We choose—

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: We decide, before calamity strikes, what shape our city is going to greet its ruin in.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: We set out to make our progeny marvel at the fruits of our technology, to make them gasp at the traces we've left behind, to make them toast with their finest tipple to all our achievements.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Just as we find other fallen cities, and do the very same.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Of course we're sad to have to leave where we grew, but it's a sadness we're accustomed to.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: And in said times for us, upkeeping our city such that it's in best condition becomes more meaningful than ever, doesn't it?

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: It's the body. It's what we call dressing our doomed city.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: It's such a... romantic notion.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Of course it is. The more straightforward reason is, we can build a brand new city in as quickly a few months, provided we bring the key industrial equipment and have our robots assisting.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: We'd never have the resources to spare for this otherwise.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Haha. Yes, good point.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Er, is that... Stitch over there?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: This one... no.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: This one? Also no.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: This one—er, what's this doing here? I'll take it with me later.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: This book? It's a Kazimierzian knight novel... Is it yours?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Ah, right, you can at least tell what that one is. It slipped my mind...

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I suppose it is. I brought it from the surface.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: About that...

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: How exactly did a lone Ursus like you wander all the way from Ursus to a Durin city?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: My family all died in a noble conflict that had absolutely no honor to speak of, and I was forced to flee from my home.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Assassins trailed me throughout my escape, until I eventually fled into a cavern.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Its structure was as complex as the one above the lift here, and I happened to find such a lift that led underground.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: And that's how I had the fortune to survive. It was that simple.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Oh, that sure was pretty lucky.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Do you have no other thoughts?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Were you hoping for any?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: ...*sigh* No wonder you're a friend of Gavial's.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: I've heard a lot of stories similar to yours aboard Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: You're already lucky enough just to have survived.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Zeruertza's a good place. It'd be pretty nice, living somewhere like this.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: It is.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I thought, originally, I'd be a lot angrier about the circumstances I'd landed in.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: But had my family really been so guiltless, my parents so benevolent in their day-to-day, simply befallen by wicked men's hate?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Of course not.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: My father still cursed his antagonists more than he cared for his own family, right until his final moments.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: As I fled out from the back of our home, I knew nothing of even the whereabouts of my mother.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: And I—I was no more than an insignificant sacrifice in a sea of Ursus noble conspiracy.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: You're right, I'm very lucky. That's why I have to cherish this hard-won luck as well as I can.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: For sure.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: You're cruising to pick a huge argument with Gavial, am I right?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: What gives you that idea?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Because she might've talked you over, but thinking about it carefully, you never actually said what you really wanted to say.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: And you tried to argue with her again, but then you lost the opportunity, so your only choice was to bite your tongue.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: I've seen a lot of people pissed off by Gavial's whole personality—she gets me too, sometimes—and you're the most obvious kind about it.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Alright, I admit it.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I've never met anyone like Gavial. Whether I'm Ursus or Durin, getting a handle on her is... elusive.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: If there's something you need to get off your mind, you can tell me. You've helped me out. I'll think about passing it onto her for you.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I'll refrain. I'm not in straits that desperate yet.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: However, I do have a proposal.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I have no plans to formally make a return to surface life.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Once the danger is past, I'll be proposing the Durins return underground.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Of course, contact can never be easily severed once made, and so breaking off dealings will be nigh-impossible. I recognize that much.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: And I admit that you, the Tiacauh of Acahualla, may be possible relational targets.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Thus, once the Durins rebuild their city underground, I'll invite you all to relocate from a rainforest void of anything, to the land beneath the surface.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: At that point, I'm sure even one of Gavial's nature will understand just how wonderful Durin society is.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Hmm... yeah, we'll pass.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Let's get back to that once we find the map.
